candidates.source_name: TED — Tenders Electronic Daily (EU official procurement journal, EN interface)
candidates.why_relevant: Above-threshold Hungarian public-sector and state-owned-bank contracts must be published EU-wide here. Contract award notices name the winning vendor, contract value, duration and CPV subject matter — the single richest deterministic source for HU banking/payments vendor and competitor wins.
candidates.legal_status: official EU publication, open reuse under EU Publications Office reuse policy
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use the official Search API / bulk XML rather than HTML scraping; filter country=HU, notice type = contract award, CPV in the payments/IT set.
queries_used: TED europa.eu Hungary contract award notice CPV 66133000 payment processing

candidates.source_name: TED — Hungarian-language interface (TED – Uniós tenderek, a Hivatalos Lap kiegészítése)
candidates.why_relevant: Same corpus as TED EN but rendered in Hungarian; Hungarian notice text carries the original procuring-entity names, lot descriptions and product wording (e.g. 'bankkártya elfogadás', 'önkiszolgáló kioszk') that the EN translation flattens. Mandatory for local-language matching of vendor/product terms.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Fetch the HU language rendition of each notice id found via the API (notice/{id} with /hu/ locale) to capture original Hungarian wording alongside EN.
queries_used: TED Magyarország hirdetmény CPV 48800000 információs rendszerek szerződés odaítéléséről

candidates.why_relevant: Machine-readable expert-query access to the whole TED corpus, no authentication required for search according to the docs. This is the collection backbone for the whole cell: deterministic CPV + country + notice-type filters, repeatable on a schedule.
candidates.legal_status: covered by TED fair-usage policy for reusers
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled expert-query calls, e.g. country=HUN AND CPV in (66133000,66172000,48800000,48730000,72000000,30200000,30123600) AND notice-type=contract-award; persist raw JSON/XML.
queries_used: TED europa.eu API documentation search notices bulk download data.europa.eu TED CSV

candidates.why_relevant: Full historical archive of notices in XML, including award history that national portals purge. Enables retrospective vendor-share reconstruction for Hungarian banking/payments CPVs over many years without hammering the search API.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off historical backfill of monthly packages, then incremental daily packages; parse XML and index by country + CPV.
queries_used: TED europa.eu API documentation search notices bulk download data.europa.eu TED CSV

candidates.source_name: TED CPV vocabulary reference (Fő és kiegészítő közös közbeszerzési szójegyzék)
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative bilingual CPV code list; gives the exact Hungarian label for each code so queries and downstream classification use the official term rather than a guess. Essential to build the checklist-free CPV slice for this cell.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Download once, store as a HU/EN CPV lookup table used to label all harvested notices.
queries_used: TED Magyarország hirdetmény CPV 48800000 információs rendszerek szerződés odaítéléséről

candidates.source_name: EU Open Data Portal — TED dataset (data.europa.eu)
candidates.why_relevant: Curated CSV/XML redistributions of TED with long historical coverage, easier to load into analysis than raw notice XML. Useful as a cross-check and for quick country+CPV aggregate counts.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic dataset download; use as reconciliation layer against API pulls. Exact dataset slug should be re-confirmed on the portal.
queries_used: TED europa.eu API documentation search notices bulk download data.europa.eu TED CSV

candidates.source_name: Opentender.eu — Hungary portal (Government Transparency Institute / DIGIWHIST)
candidates.why_relevant: Merges TED above-threshold data with the Hungarian national portal (Közbeszerzési Hatóság) below-threshold data into structured, comparable records with buyer/supplier entities and red-flag indicators. Lets us see the same vendors below the EU threshold, which TED alone misses.
candidates.legal_status: research project open data; check per-dataset licence
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Bulk download from the all-data page, filter country HU, then join supplier names to our vendor/competitor entity list.
queries_used: opentender.eu Hungary procurement data DIGIWHIST tenders EU-funded contract awards

candidates.source_name: Open Contracting Partnership Data Registry — Hungary / TED publications
candidates.why_relevant: Registry describing what procurement data exists for Hungary and the EU, in what format, with what coverage and update cadence. A pointer source that reveals additional publishers and OCDS endpoints we would not find by direct search.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Manual review once per quarter to detect new/changed Hungarian publishers; harvest linked endpoints.
queries_used: opentender.eu Hungary procurement data DIGIWHIST tenders EU-funded contract awards

candidates.source_name: Government Transparency Institute (govtransparency.eu) — tools and methodology
candidates.why_relevant: Documents how the Hungarian procurement data is scraped, cleaned and entity-matched; the methodology tells us which fields are reliable and which HU-specific quirks (buyer name variants, entity IDs) must be normalised before vendor-share analysis.
queries_used: opentender.eu Hungary procurement data DIGIWHIST tenders EU-funded contract awards

candidates.source_name: Kohesio — EU Cohesion policy project and beneficiary database
candidates.why_relevant: EU-funded contract/project award database covering ERDF, CF, ESF+, JTF for 2014-2020 and 2021-2027, searchable by country and beneficiary. Hungarian digitalisation, fintech and public-sector IT projects appear with beneficiary names and amounts — an EU-level route to Hungarian buyer/vendor activity that never reaches TED.
candidates.legal_status: official EU platform, open reuse; full country exports offered
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Download the Hungary project and beneficiary exports; also query the EU Knowledge Graph SPARQL endpoint referenced in their FAQ.
queries_used: Kohesio EU cohesion data Hungary projects database ERDF beneficiaries search

candidates.why_relevant: Recipients of directly/indirectly managed EU funds, searchable by beneficiary country. Captures Hungarian entities (including banks, IT vendors, consultancies) receiving EU contracts and grants that are not in shared-management national systems.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual dataset download filtered to beneficiary country = Hungary; keyword-match on payments/IT/security subject fields.
queries_used: EU Financial Transparency System recipients database ec.europa.eu budget FTS search

candidates.source_name: Közbeszerzési Hatóság — Közbeszerzési Értesítő (Hungarian Public Procurement Bulletin)
candidates.why_relevant: National counterpart to TED: every domestic notice, including below-threshold awards, in Hungarian. Cross-referencing TED notice ids against the Értesítő gives the fuller Hungarian award picture and the original Hungarian buyer/vendor spellings.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use the notice search database endpoint with CPV and keyword filters; archive the PDF notices, which are stable long-lived URLs.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search + snowball from TED HU notices
queries_used: "Közbeszerzési Értesítő" kozbeszerzes.hu hirdetmény kereső EKR ekr.gov.hu eljárás bankkártya terminál

candidates.source_name: EKR — Elektronikus Közbeszerzési Rendszer (Hungarian e-procurement system) notices
candidates.why_relevant: The operational system where Hungarian procedures actually run since 2018; procedure documentation, technical specifications and clarification Q&A are attached per procedure. Technical annexes are where competitor product names, HSM/terminal specs and integration requirements surface.
candidates.access_status: public listing; some documents may require registration
candidates.legal_status: official state platform; respect terms of use
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor the public notices list, resolve procedure ids found in TED HU notices, download public procedure documents. Expect session/anti-bot handling — treat failures as unverified, not dead.
queries_used: "Közbeszerzési Értesítő" kozbeszerzes.hu hirdetmény kereső EKR ekr.gov.hu eljárás bankkártya terminál

candidates.source_name: Támogatott Projektkereső — palyazat.gov.hu (Hungarian EU-funded project search)
candidates.why_relevant: National register of EU-funded awarded projects (Széchenyi Terv Plusz, Széchenyi 2020, RRF/Helyreállítási és Ellenállóképességi Terv), fed daily from EMIR/EUPR/IIER. Reveals which Hungarian banks, savings institutions and IT firms got EU money for digitalisation projects — strong lead generator for case studies and partnerships.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Filtered exports by operational programme and beneficiary category; keyword-scan project titles for payments/IT/security terms; archive because older periods migrate to archive.palyazat.gov.hu.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search (who publishes EU-fund beneficiaries nationally)
queries_used: palyazat.gov.hu támogatott projektkereső Széchenyi 2020 EU-s támogatás kedvezményezettek adatbázis

candidates.why_relevant: KÖFOP is the Hungarian operational programme funding public administration IT — the programme behind much state digital/payment infrastructure. Project-level base data identifies the implementing state bodies whose downstream tenders appear in TED under IT and security CPVs.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic download of the published project tables; join implementing-body names to TED buyer names.
queries_used: palyazat.gov.hu támogatott projektkereső Széchenyi 2020 EU-s támogatás kedvezményezettek adatbázis

candidates.source_name: EBRD Client e-Procurement Portal (ECEPP) and contract award notifications
candidates.why_relevant: IFI-funded contract awards outside the EU-directive regime. EBRD finances Hungarian financial-sector and infrastructure clients; award notifications name suppliers and contract values, covering deals that never enter TED.
candidates.access_status: public listing; registration needed to participate
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor the notices and contract-award pages filtered to Hungary; low volume, so a weekly poll suffices.
candidates.discovered_via_method: first-principles (who else funds and must publish awards)
queries_used: EBRD EIB procurement notices Hungary bank IT contract award database

candidates.source_name: EU Publications Office — TED reusers workshops Q&A and eForms retrieval guides
candidates.why_relevant: Explains the eForms migration, field-level semantics and retrieval patterns. Without this, award-value and winner fields are easy to misparse across the pre-2024 TED schema and the eForms era — a correctness risk for any HU vendor-share metric.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Read-once; re-check when TED announces schema changes.
queries_used: TED europa.eu API documentation search notices bulk download data.europa.eu TED CSV

candidates.why_relevant: Older Hungarian notices are still reachable via the legacy udl permalink pattern with an explicit HU language token — important for historical backfill because some archive links surface only in this form. Example found: a Hungary-Budapest information-system strategy services notice.
candidates.access_status: public; legacy URLs may redirect to the new notice viewer
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use as a fallback resolver when the modern /notice/{id} path fails; follow redirects rather than recording the notice as dead.
queries_used: TED Magyarország hirdetmény CPV 48800000 információs rendszerek szerződés odaítéléséről

candidates.source_name: Commercial TED/EU tender aggregators (TendersOnTime, GlobalTenders, Apify TED scraper)
candidates.why_relevant: Secondary aggregators that sometimes surface IFI and non-TED notices in a searchable form and can act as a discovery shortcut. Low credibility as a primary record — always resolve back to the official notice before using a fact.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Manual discovery use only; do not scrape. Resolve every lead to the official TED/EBRD notice.
queries_used: EBRD EIB procurement notices Hungary bank IT contract award database
candidates.observed_blocker: Aggregator sites gate full notice text behind registration/subscription and prohibit automated reuse in their terms.

negative_findings.description: Searches for Hungarian TED notices under CPV 66133000 (processing and clearing services) returned CPV-matching award notices, but the examples surfaced were French rather than Hungarian.
negative_findings.result_summary: Could not evidence a specific Hungarian 66133000 award from search alone; this CPV may be rarely used by Hungarian buyers, who may classify payment work under IT services CPVs instead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A CPV-only slice keyed on 66133000 would under-cover Hungary. The CPV set must be widened to IT services (72xxxxxx), software/information systems (488xxxxx) and equipment (30xxxxxx) and verified against the actual TED API rather than a search engine.

negative_findings.description: No Hungarian TED notice under CPV 30123600 (cash dispensers / bankjegykiadó automaták) was located via search; results were journalistic coverage of the MNB-mandated ATM rollout instead.
negative_findings.result_summary: ATM procurement in Hungary appears to be driven by commercial banks and a regulator-mandated programme rather than by public tender, so it may be largely absent from TED.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Self-service/ATM competitive intelligence for Hungary probably cannot rely on TED and needs a different workstream (regulator publications, bank disclosures, vendor press).

negative_findings.description: No Hungary-specific EU-level notice was found for CPV 48730000 (security software / HSM) in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: The HSM/security-software slice produced no verifiable Hungarian example within this run's search budget.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Security/HSM is a core Printec-adjacent category; absence of evidence here is a search-budget limitation, not proof of absence, and must be re-tested directly against the TED API.

negative_findings.description: The TED bulk-download page, the TED API swagger endpoint, the data.europa.eu TED dataset slug and the EU Knowledge Graph query service for Kohesio were all cited in documentation but not fetched in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: URLs recorded from official documentation; liveness and exact paths not confirmed here.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass must confirm these before they are wired into a collector; a stale dataset slug would silently produce empty harvests.

coverage_gaps.description: The mapping from banking/payments subject matter to actual CPV codes used by Hungarian buyers has not been empirically validated — it is currently an assumption.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a TED API frequency analysis: all HU notices for the last 5 years, count CPV codes among notices whose title/description matches a HU/EN payments-and-banking keyword list, and derive the CPV slice from the data instead of a priori.

coverage_gaps.description: TED and EU-funded award databases cover public buyers. Commercial Hungarian banks (OTP, K&H, Erste, Raiffeisen, MBH, UniCredit, CIB) procure payments technology privately and appear only when state-owned or EU-cofunded.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Flag to the coordinating agent that private-bank vendor intelligence needs a different cell (vendor press releases, bank annual reports, MNB publications); do not treat TED coverage as market coverage.

coverage_gaps.description: Hungarian supplier names in TED/EKR appear with varying legal-form suffixes (Kft., Zrt., Nyrt., Bt.), accents and consortium constructions; no normalisation or tax-number join has been designed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a HU entity-normalisation step keyed on adószám/cégjegyzékszám where present, and reuse Opentender's entity-matching output as a starting dictionary.

coverage_gaps.description: Much Hungarian public IT buying runs through central purchasing bodies and framework agreements (központosított közbeszerzés, keretmegállapodás), where the TED award names the framework holder and the real call-offs are invisible.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Identify the Hungarian central purchasing body's framework registers and call-off reporting, and treat framework awards as pointers to be resolved rather than as final contract values.

coverage_gaps.description: Hungarian national portals migrate content (archive.palyazat.gov.hu already exists as a separate archive host), so links captured today may move.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Snapshot every harvested Hungarian notice/project record locally at collection time and store the retrieval date; do not rely on live national URLs for provenance.

brief: For Hungary, the EU-level procurement layer is dominated by one authoritative spine — TED, reachable through its HTML portal in both English and Hungarian, a no-auth Search API, and daily/monthly XML bulk packages that preserve award history national portals purge. Around it sit three useful rings: a research aggregator layer (Opentender/DIGIWHIST, OCP registry) that fuses TED with below-threshold Hungarian data from the Közbeszerzési Hatóság; the national originals (Közbeszerzési Értesítő and EKR) where the Hungarian-language technical annexes and product specs actually live; and EU-funded award databases (Kohesio, the Financial Transparency System, and Hungary's own Támogatott Projektkereső plus KÖFOP tables) that expose digitalisation projects and beneficiaries never tendered EU-wide. The main structural caveat is that a CPV-keyed slice is only as good as the CPV codes Hungarian buyers actually use — 66133000 produced no verified Hungarian example in this pass, and ATM procurement appears to sit outside public tendering entirely — so the CPV set should be derived empirically from the TED API before any collector is fixed. Commercial banks remain a deliberate blind spot of this cell and must be covered elsewhere.
